summary: Ordinary attestation identity (attestation_id_for) hashes only the draft while stored equality includes created_by_run, so equal evidence from two independent runs collides.
failure_scenario: Two valid leased runs with identical sealed ExecutionManifest (manifest_hash is not run-unique) mint an identical merge/promote draft -> first mint inserts, second derives the same id, _stored_attestation_for_draft finds created_by_run mismatch and raises JournalDamaged; benign independent evidence is reported as journal corruption and the second run's gate/evaluation fails.
evidence: Reproduced with fakes only (scratch script, no repo edits): create_test_run run-a/run-b -> manifests equal=True; promote draft: run-a mints, run-a re-mint is idempotent (True), run-b mint raises JournalDamaged 'already minted with different content'; same for a MergeSubject draft. Root: effect.py:173 digest('attestation',1,draft) vs _sqlite_execution.py:960-975 expected Attestation(created_by_run=...). Pre-existing (baseline).

summary: A run holding any lease can pre-mint (squat) the id of an identical future draft and make another run's mint fail with JournalDamaged; no cross-run isolation of the id namespace.
failure_scenario: Run A (same graph/inputs hence same manifest_hash) mints draft D for subject S; later run B legitimately computes D and gets JournalDamaged permanently (the row is append-only). Failure class is damage rather than a refusal, so recovery/diagnostics may treat the journal as corrupt.
evidence: Follows from the reproduced collision; ids are fully derivable from public draft fields. Squatting variant by a distinct-owner lease not separately executed beyond the two-run repro.

summary: The 'return the prior attestation' alternative (relaxing equality to ignore created_by_run) is unsafe: it hands run B another run's proof.
failure_scenario: If B received A's attestation, downstream consumers that require created_by_run == run_id (plan_manifest_application.py:418, _qualification_write_report.py:370, maintenance_diagnostic.py:295), promotion_attestation_faults source_run binding (effect.py:239), validated_channel_send_attestation, _require_current_creator and RUN_CHILD_ORPHAN_ANOMALY run-world joins would refuse or mis-attribute provenance (promotion source_run would name A for B's evidence).
evidence: Read each consumer; they all compare created_by_run to the consuming run. Not executed (design rejection).

summary: Any run-scoped identity needs a versioned reader law; the reader currently derives ids only from the run-less draft and treats every other mismatch as damage, so a naive writer-only change makes new rows undecodable and a naive reader-accepts-both change makes post-migration v1 run-owned rows indistinguishable from historical ones.
failure_scenario: If mint writes run-scoped ids but _stored_attestation_from_json (lines 78-100), the constructicon_attestation_id UDF and stored_attestation_for_id keep v1-only derivation, every new row raises ValueError->JournalDamaged on read/seal/inventory. If readers accept v1 for any created_by_run forever, a later bug/tamper writing a v1-id run-owned row would be accepted as 'content-derived' with no era seal, contradicting ADR0016 closed named eras.
evidence: Read the reader, _fact_family (provenance only m1-m2 | content-derived) and the migration reseal loop (_sqlite_schema.py:940, SCHEMA_VERSION=9). Design analysis; not executed.

summary: Adding created_by_run (or an actor/command field) to AttestationDraft would silently change every existing id and persisted plan hash.
failure_scenario: AttestationDraft is serialized into sealed promotion/rollback plans and hashed by attestation_id_for(model_dump); a new field, even defaulting to None, alters model_dump(mode='json') so all v1 ids and policy plan drafts (registry.py:883/939, _control_commands.py:3207) stop deriving and run-less policy semantics change.
evidence: attestation_id_for hashes draft.model_dump(mode='json') directly (effect.py:173-175). Not executed.

summary: Run-less policy attestations share the v1 id namespace with run-owned ones, so a run mint of a byte-equal promote draft can collide with (or squat) a policy id.
failure_scenario: Policy draft (manifest_hash, checks, evidence) equal to a run's ordinary promote draft -> whichever is minted first wins; the other gets JournalDamaged. Likely rare because policy drafts carry policy-specific checks.
evidence: Code reading of mint_policy_attestation vs mint_attestation; same collision mechanism, policy side not executed.

summary: Recommended minimal design (owner decision A): run-owned ordinary attestations get a versioned, run-scoped id: attestation_id_for_run(draft, run_id)=digest('attestation',2,{'draft':draft_dump,'created_by_run':run_id}) with the same 'att-' prefix; run-less policy attestations keep v1 unchanged (ids are baked into sealed plans and accepted M6.2 semantics). Scratch prototype (not repo code): v1, v2(run-a), v2(run-b) are three distinct ids, so the two-run repro would mint two rows. digest() domain-separates by version so v1/v2 cannot collide.

Readers (owner decision B): derive by created_by_run: null -> v1 only; non-null -> v2 for new rows, v1 accepted only for rows carrying a migration-written era seal (e.g. family attestation_run_v1_pre_vN, same mechanism as legacy_attestation_m1_m2, provenance literal extended). Update _stored_attestation_from_json, _fact_family, seal/require/inventory, UDFs and the dual-family contradiction checks together. Pure read-time acceptance of v1 for all run-owned rows is rejected (tamper-indistinguishable).

Migration (owner decision C): bump SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 9) so older binaries refuse v2 rows instead of marking them damaged; migration must not rewrite existing rows or ids (immutable historical proofs, promotions/effects/channel_messages reference them), only add era seals to existing run-owned v1 rows. Fresh DBs write v2 only.

Same-run mint idempotence must remain: _stored_attestation_for_draft computes the run-scoped id, compares full stored equality ignoring created_at (crash-retry before time observation), and keeps JournalDamaged for genuine content mismatch under the same id; _insert_attestation prior-equality guard and collision guards stay unchanged (do not weaken same_definition/collision guards).

Independent runs with equal evidence become independent attestations with distinct ids and correct created_by_run, so merge/promote consumers (created_by_run == run_id checks, promotion source_run derivation, send subject carrying run_id) keep working unmodified. One-attestation/one-promotion receipt replay is unchanged per id: a second run's attestation for the same edge hits normal stable-moved CAS refusal (AdmissionError) rather than silently replaying run A's receipt; this is intended explicit semantics and should be stated in the ADR/plan addendum (owner decision D, ADR edit outside this review).

Rejected alternatives: (1) add created_by_run to AttestationDraft: changes all v1 ids and plan bytes; (2) return prior row across runs: breaks provenance (see finding); (3) composite key (attestation_id, created_by_run): breaks every single-id reference (promotions, effects, channel_messages, load_attestation, approvals); (4) explicit replay-by-flag on mint: reintroduces caller-selected authority. Only run-scoped versioned ids preserve manifest/check-set/evidence binding and run provenance.

Public schema impact: AttestationDraft and Attestation wire shapes unchanged; only the id derivation function and its reader law change. Ordinary gate writers (runner.py:249, contained.py:439, walker.py:160) need no call-site change because mint_attestation already receives the lease; send attestations already include run_id in the subject.

Test matrix (proof obligations): (a) two runs identical manifest+draft mint two distinct rows, each created_by_run correct, both pass seal inventory and reopen; (b) same-run re-mint idempotent with clock that refuses time observation; (c) tampered row: v2 id with wrong created_by_run, v1 id on post-migration run-owned row without era seal, run-owned row id swapped between runs -> JournalDamaged; (d) migration of a v9 DB with pre-existing run-owned v1 rows keeps ids, adds era seals, leaves promotions/effects referencing them valid, and old-binary/schema gate refuses; (e) policy run-less draft still maps to v1 and equals planned id in registry.py/_control_commands.py plans; (f) refusal path: run B minting after run A's lease lost still gets OwnershipLost, manifest mismatch ContractViolation (guards reached); (g) promotion of same edge by two run attestations: first succeeds, second refused stable-moved, receipt replay for the same id returns first receipt; (h) mutant check: removing created_by_run from the v2 body must fail (a).

Existing test tests/substrate/journal/test_attestation_idempotency.py covers same-run retries and tampering of identity fields only (_ATTESTATION_IDENTITY_FIELDS); no case mints equal drafts from two runs, which is why the baseline defect is not caught. Failure semantics for the fix: independent-run equal evidence must never raise JournalDamaged; JournalDamaged remains only for same-id/different-content or undecodable rows.
